correctness.rationale: For ordinary area measure the half-plane Berezin probability has density 4(Im u)^2/(π|u−conj(v)|^4). Straightening the genuine sector by w^p and reflecting gives an analytic chart with nonzero positive derivative in the straightened coordinate, so hσ(v)=c^(−s)|v|^s(1+O(|v|)) near zero, s=σ/p. For fixed interior u the small-radius integral has exponent s+1: divergence at s≤−2 is at every evaluation point. On an interior angular compactum, |u−conj(v)| is bounded below by a fixed multiple of |u|+|v|. Consequently the rescaled middle integrand is dominated by a constant times |v|^s/(1+|v|)^4, and the part away from the mapped corner is of order r^(2p). At s=2, on 2|u|<|v|<ε the relative errors O(|v|)+O(|u|/|v|) have bounded integrals against d|v|/|v|; the angular measure π and the radial logarithm p log(1/r) give 4p sin²(pφ), with the two complementary regions bounded after division by r^(2p). For s>2 the integrable majorant hσ(v)|v|^(−4) gives the asserted saturated coefficient, with no need for hσ to have bounded support in the half-plane. Under a change ψ(v)=λv/(1+bv) the Jacobian ratio |ψ′(v)|²/|ψ(v)|⁴=λ^(−2)|v|^(−4) cancels the change in c². Reflection gives angular symmetry; off any neighborhood of the relevant side point ±1 the weighted kernel mass tends to zero, using the same two integrability exponents. At the bisector the Cayley map gives uniform disk area, q↦−q negates the logarithm X, and its disk orthogonality variance is 2∑_{n odd}1/[n²(n+1)]=π²/4−2log 2. Strict Jensen and a Taylor expansion justified by exponential moments in |s|<2 give both bisector claims.
residual_risks: Uniformity requires a fixed interior angular compactum; no assertion for simultaneous side-tangential approach. The extended integral is not a bounded Toeplitz operator assertion.
